chunks: Al-Ḥalabī and ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
May a man recite in his salat (prayer) while his garment is over his mouth? He said: "There is no harm in that."
And in the narration of al-Ḥalabī: "If he hears the murmuring."

key_terms.الْهَمْهَمَةَ: the low murmuring sound of recitation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.يَقْرَأُ: recites or reads aloud in the context of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can a person recite in salat (prayer) while his garment covers his mouth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about recitation in salat (prayer) while the mouth is covered by a garment. The ruling permits it, and the additional wording indicates that the recitation remains valid when the person can hear his own murmuring.
